column1: # and what the downstream contract owes for it. Enforced by the SV-CONTRACT-CURRENCY doctrine
# ⛔ WHY IT EXISTS, measured not imagined: between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-19 the SV grammar shipped
# SEVEN semantically-distinct revisions while the contract kept saying `1.0.183`. The leaf that
# opened to fix that debt tracked the population BY HAND and its table went stale twice more inside
# the same week — `-0232` and `-0233` landed and were never added, so `-0237` was routed as "the
# FIFTH change" when it was the SEVENTH commit and the FIFTH to move a verdict. A hand-kept list of
# accept-set changes is the same object as the debt it tracks.
# semantic_digest = sha256 of the EBNF FRONTEND'S OWN `raw_ast` envelope — what the code generator
# consumes, from which comments are absent by construction. Re-derive:
# ⛔ To a FILE, never /dev/stdout — the tool writes progress there too and the JSON parse fails.
# ⛔ THE KEY IS THE DIGEST, NOT THE COMMIT. The first design keyed rows on the commit sha and had a
# chicken-and-egg the very next grammar change exposed: the row for the commit being made cannot
# carry that commit's own sha. The digest is known BEFORE the commit is, and it is the identity the
# contract actually describes, so `commit` is documentation and may be back-filled.
# disposition: RELEASE = the contract carries a section and the bug ledger carries a row.
#              NEUTRAL = comment-only; the digest EQUALS its predecessor's, which is what the
#              doctrine checks, so the claim refutes itself when false.
#              GENERATOR-ONLY = the digest MOVED and the generated PARSER did not. The revision
#              touches generation-side annotation text only (`@sample`), so the accept set and the
#              AST cannot have moved and no consumer of the parser can observe it. Ships no release,
#              owes no ledger row, and carries `parser_sha256=<64 hex>` in its notes; tier E hashes
#              generated/systemverilog_parser.rs and refuses on any difference.
#              ⛔ Added by SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.9 because a real change fit NEITHER existing slot: a
#              `@sample` repair moves the digest (annotations are in the raw_ast, comments are not),
#              so NEUTRAL refutes itself — while RELEASE would have bought its currency check with a
#              bug-ledger row describing a defect no released parser has. A vocabulary with a hole
#              in it does not fail loudly; it gets the nearest wrong label.
# ⛔ frontend_rekey: the digest is the FRONTEND'S reading of the grammar, so a frontend change re-keys every
# earlier row without a grammar byte moving. Each line below names the LAST commit whose rows were keyed by the
# reading before such a change; tier A does not re-derive commits at or before it (they are HISTORY, re-derivable
# only with the frontend of their day), and prints how many it skipped. EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION.6
# (2026-09-03): comments cut out of annotation payloads + `//` read as the meta-grammar's line comment.

SV-0066 (.13c.2y) -- an IEEE 1800 KEYWORD was bound to the ARROW token of the same name: `implies := trivia "->"` predated the extraction of A.2.10, so `a implies b` was REJECTED at every release while `-> b` and `a |= b` parsed as properties. Minted kw_implies_470cec58 (profile-gated SV-only) and moved the operator to its Table 16-3 precedence group prop_until_*, deleting three defect branches from both prop_primary_*. SV-0068 (.13e.5) -- IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.7 makes a task/function port DIRECTION mandatory (task_port_item is one of three tf_*_declarations, each BEGINNING with its keyword), and PGEN carried the IEEE 1800 shape (direction optional) on ALL profiles, so `task t(a, b);` parsed as plain Verilog. NARROW on verilog_2005 only: `tf_port_item`/`tf_port_list` split into profile-gated variants; the sv_2017/sv_2023 body is a byte-for-byte re-spelling. ⛔ The obvious fix (a direction on EVERY item) was built, regenerated and MEASURED rejecting `task t(input integer a, b);`, which A.2.7:300 DERIVES -- one `input` covers a list_of_port_identifiers -- so the shipped shape admits a directionless item only when it is a BARE port identifier and requires the FIRST item to carry a direction. Schema 26 unchanged (both variants emit the identical 5-field return; ast_shape_contract 18/18, drift 0).

SV-0069 (.13e.4) -- IEEE 1364-2005 puts NO signing on an integer or a time declaration: A.2.1.3 integer_declaration:152 and time_declaration:174 are `<kw> list_of_variable_identifiers ;`, A.2.8's block forms :314/:315 are the same, and neither `signing` nor `integer_atom_type` appears anywhere in that Annex. PGEN spelled `data_type` and `block_data_type` the IEEE 1800 way -- `integer_atom_type ( signing )?` -- with NO @profiles gate, so `integer unsigned u;` / `time signed t;` parsed as plain Verilog at module, block, function and task scope. NARROW on verilog_2005 only. ⭐ THE GATE GOES ON THE OPTIONAL, NOT ON THE ALTERNATIVE: unlike SV-0068, the rule beside it (`integer_atom_type`) MUST stay reachable under verilog_2005 -- that admission is what makes plain `integer i;` parse -- so the .13e.5 _sv_only/_v2005 split is the wrong idiom here. One new rule `integer_atom_signing_sv_only := signing` @profiles [sv_2017, sv_2023], referenced inside the optional at both sites: no data_type alternative added, no branch index moved, `signing: $2` keeps its slot and is simply always absent under verilog_2005. ⛔ The routing evidence understated the defect TWICE and one command said so each time -- `time` is the same atom (integer_atom_type admits exactly integer + time under this profile) and `block_data_type:2077` is a second byte-identical site. Schema 26 unchanged (the sv_2017 typed AST is byte-identical across the edit, proven on 11 inputs by --interpret-parse-ast-json BEFORE any codegen).

SV-0070 (.13e.7) -- IEEE 1364-2005 admits none of thirteen IEEE-1800 surfaces the verilog_2005 profile was still reaching, and the population was MEASURED over a closed set rather than listed: `chandle`/`enum`/`string`/`virtual interface` types (each occurs 0x in Annex A; `string` is the A.8.8:1218 LITERAL, never a type), the `const`/`var` qualifiers and the DATA-declaration and MODULE-header `lifetime` (A.2.1.3:152 carries no qualifier and no lifetime; A.1.2:29 no lifetime at all), `extern` on a module or UDP header, `default disable iff`, `fork join_any` / `join_none` (A.6.3 par_block:529 -- `join` is the ONLY terminator), the checker `rand` qualifier, the array-method `with` clause, and the whole streaming concatenation (`{ << { a } }`, which no keyword-level lens can see because `<<` and `>>` are OPERATORS). Fixed with the named `_sv_only` idiom at 19 v2005-live sites plus one whole-rule gate on `streaming_concatenation`; `lifetime` itself stays UNGATED because A.2.6:254 / A.2.7:275 give function/task a legitimate `[automatic]`. ACCEPT-SET NARROW under verilog_2005 ONLY: sv_2017 and sv_2023 are byte-identical (each gate is a bare pass-through alias and the reference site keeps its return annotation), ast_shape_contract 18/18 with the AST schema UNCHANGED, sv_cert union total 1388->1401 / union_witness 1380->1393 (+13 = exactly the rules added) with union_unknown still 0.

Both are IEEE-1800-only; IEEE 1364-2005 spells them `wire` and `integer`, and BOTH repairs parse under all three profiles (measured both directions with --interpret-parse). A @sample is one profile-blind string, so every witness probe short-circuiting through one emitted a file verilog_2005 must reject: 5608 of the 5776 parsed=false probe samples at seed 0 carried `input logic`, and 0 of those 5608 ever parsed. The generated parser moved under ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.46 (c) (a negative lookahead's body is now evaluated with @profiles gating ignored where it would otherwise be vacuous), which has nothing to do with this grammar revision, so tier E's pin went stale as designed. ⭐ The row's CLAIM was then re-derived rather than assumed: regenerating grammars/systemverilog.ebnf at 2e492d08^ and at 2e492d08 with the repaired codegen -- holding the grammar BASENAME and the -o PATH constant, because the emitted parser embeds both -- yields byte-identical output hashing to this value, so the GENERATOR-ONLY disposition still holds. ⚠️ Nothing in the check FORCED that re-derivation; see ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.48, which owns giving the re-stamp a producer. The prose sha256 earlier in this row is left at 8bc4746aeb0363e9... deliberately: it records what the artifact hashed to when the row was written, which is history rather than a live claim.

SV-0071 (.13e.10(c4)) -- SIXTEEN IEEE-1800-only OPERATORS still reached the verilog_2005 profile, and the class was invisible to every census that preceded it: the .13e.7 instrument crosses profile-filtered reachability against IEEE 1364-2005 Annex B, a normative list of KEYWORDS, so a construct spelled entirely in PUNCTUATION can never become a candidate. The twelve compound assignments (`+= -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>= <<<= >>>=`, A.6.2 gives `=` and `<=` and nothing else) reach v2005 through `assignment_operator`; the three comparison/equivalence forms (`==? !=? <->`, A.8.6 defines none of them) through `binary_operator`; and `.*` (A.4.1 named_port_connection has no implicit form) through 7 hosts every one of which is NAMED `_sv_2017` while exactly THREE are @profiles-ADMITTED to verilog_2005 -- .13e.7's root cause verbatim, a naming convention is not an enforcement mechanism. Fixed with 16 whole-rule @profiles gates on the TERMINALS themselves, the SV-0031 `scope_resolution` idiom: gating the token root prunes the class in one place, where retagging the three mis-admitted hosts would not and would break legal Verilog. LRM evidence RE-DERIVED not carried: 13 of the 16 occur ZERO times in the whole in-repo IEEE 1364-2005 corpus; `+=`/`-=` occur only inside the clause-14 specify-path polarity operators `+=>`/`-=>`, `.*` only as a clause-13 library-map filename glob. The raw_ast digest is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its predecessor `b744a239bf8e5053...` -- the frontend strips comments, verified by re-deriving the envelope before and after the edit -- so the generated parser on disk is still exactly what this grammar produces and no regeneration is owed. SV-0072 (.13e.10(c4) RESIDUE, ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.50(e) + .55) -- THE SEVENTEENTH IEEE-1800-ONLY PUNCTUATION MEMBER, `'` (tick), IS GATED OUT OF verilog_2005, closing the class .13e.10 opened. It took THREE engine repairs to make ONE tag landable, and each is why the tag was deferred for a day: .50(b) -- tagging constant_cast makes its @profiles CROSS constant_primary_sv_2017's, the route intersection ['sv_2017'] is a set no rule on the route declares, and the eliminator REFUSED the whole casting_type candidate (left_recursion_unhandled 0 -> 15, a WARNING, so --lint-grammar still exited 0); it now SYNTHESIZES the intersection onto the clone. .55 -- the pass's own casting_type_lr_suffix / _lr_guard{0,1}_suffix are an ordered choice over the ROUTES and inherited @profiles from the BASE rule, which declares none, leaving them profile ORPHANS whose lint-derived fix nobody could apply because there is no source line to tag; the wrapper now takes the UNION of its branches' gates. .50(d) -- left_recursion_unhandled is now RATCHETED. *** THE COMPANION SET IS 7 SOURCE RULES, NOT THE 11 THE LINT NAMES: four are eliminator temporaries that resolve once the engine derives their gates, so the edit is 8 tags, not the 24-28 (c4) priced. *** ACCEPT-SET CHANGE, INTENDED AND TWO-SIDED: `a = '{1,2};` flips ACCEPT -> reject under verilog_2005 (the over-acceptance) while `1'b0` / `8'hff` still parse under all three profiles -- the LRM's own `'` occurrences in 1364-2005 are inside sized/based number literals, which `number` lexes and which never reach this terminal. sv_2017/sv_2023 are UNMOVED: 10/10 typed ASTs byte-identical over 5 inputs x 2 SV profiles, and the chained cast `int'(2)'(3)` still ACCEPTS on the GENERATED parser -- the observation .50(c) owed and the interpreter could not settle (TOOLBOX 1.5b marks it untrustworthy exactly when left_recursion_unhandled > 0). run_adjudication_repros went RED on EXACTLY one row with zero collateral, then checked=247 armed=81 listed=161 failures=0 after the flip. corpus_checks 360 / 0 mismatches, lint rc 0, profile_orphans 0.
